name: Brown Tourmaline
physical: Traditionally associated with a sense of stability
Crystal healers link it to digestion and steady energy
Many people keep it nearby for comfort during stressful stretches
summary: Brown Tourmaline, or dravite, is an earthy chocolate to amber stone prized for grounding, steady nerves and a calm, protective boundary around you.
intro: Brown tourmaline is tourmaline in its coziest clothes. Technically this is dravite, the magnesium-rich member of the family, and it ranges from pale honey and amber to rich chocolate and nearly black. Crystals grow as striated, three-sided columns with rounded triangular cross-sections, and they can look like tiny wooden posts or sticks of toffee. Gem-quality faceted stones glow warmly when light passes through them, and they sometimes show a golden sheen at certain angles. It is an affordable, sturdy stone, easy to wear and to carry, and a good first tourmaline for anyone who wants an earth-toned stone without the weight of black.
history: Dravite takes its name from the Drave river region in Carinthia, in what is now Austria and Slovenia, where it was first described in the 1880s. The word tourmaline itself comes from the Sinhalese toramalli, applied to colored stones from Sri Lanka. Brown tourmaline was long overshadowed by flashier pink and green varieties, though it was always used in cabochons and beads. Dutch gem traders in the 1700s reportedly used heated tourmaline to pick up ash, giving the family the nickname ash-puller, thanks to its pyroelectric nature. Today Tanzania and Kenya produce fine golden to chocolate dravite, and Brazil, Sri Lanka and Australia contribute as well.
meaning: As tourmaline in an earth tone, brown tourmaline is considered a grounding and shielding crystal. Practitioners associate it with the Root and Earth Star chakras, and use it when they feel floaty, anxious or overextended. The idea is that the stone sets a firm floor beneath you while the wider tourmaline reputation for protection acts as a soft boundary against stray moods from others. Its warm brown is also tied to home, family and tradition, so it is a favorite for people settling into a new house or working on long, slow projects. Compared with black tourmaline, it is treated as gentler and more nurturing, a stone for steadiness without heaviness.
howToUse: Keep a brown tourmaline in your pocket on crowded commutes or busy workdays. Hold a crystal in each hand while sitting on the floor, imagine roots growing from your hips into the ground, and breathe slowly for several minutes. Place a chunk by the front door, or one in each corner of a room you want to feel settled. Wear it as a ring or bracelet to keep its grounding energy with you. In a grid, set it at the base to anchor lighter stones like clear quartz. Some people sleep with a small stone on the nightstand to support winding down.
care: Brown tourmaline is hard and stable, so cleansing is easy. A quick rinse in lukewarm water, a wipe with a soft cloth, and you are done. Moonlight, sunlight, smoke and sound all suit it, and burying it in a pot of soil overnight is a fitting tradition for a grounding stone. Avoid ultrasonic cleaners and sudden temperature changes if there are fractures. Tourmaline can attract dust because of its pyroelectric charge, so wipe it every so often. Store it in a pouch away from harder gems such as sapphire.
identify: Look for the lengthwise striations on natural crystals and the rounded triangular cross-section. Dravite is doubly refractive, so a faceted stone shows doubling of back facets under magnification. Brown glass and smoky quartz are the usual look-alikes; smoky quartz is softer and lacks striations. Heat treatment occasionally lightens dark stones, and some dark tourmaline is irradiated or dyed in the trade, so be wary of unusually uniform colors at low prices. Dravite is also pyroelectric, collecting a little dust when warmed.

faq.q: What is brown tourmaline good for?
faq.a: People use brown tourmaline for grounding, steadiness and gentle protection. It is linked to the Root and Earth Star chakras and kept as a calm, down-to-earth companion during stressful days or big changes.

faq.q: Is brown tourmaline the same as dravite?
faq.a: Mostly yes. Dravite is the mineral name for magnesium-rich tourmaline, which is usually brown to yellowish-brown. Trade names can overlap, but brown tourmaline in shops is almost always dravite.

faq.q: Can brown tourmaline go in water?
faq.a: Yes, a short rinse in lukewarm water is fine. Tourmaline is hard and stable, but avoid long soaks, ultrasonic cleaners and sudden heat changes, which can stress stones with inclusions or cracks.
